summary: The candidate adds one bounded retry of a 502/503/504 GraphQL live-inputs chunk within the chunk original deadline, re-checks the cooldown gate and never retries lost, rate-limited, malformed or permanent failures; the repair regression test over fake ports shows one injected gateway fault costs one extra GraphQL request instead of fleet-wide per-record fallback, with 60 records still skipped and no state write. Thresholds and gates are untouched.

evidence: `src/github/client.ts:84-115` retries a failed live-inputs chunk only on 502/503/504, shares the original chunk deadline, disposes the parent timer, and still fails the whole read on a persistent fault.
`tests/github/client-live-inputs-retry_test.ts:55-141` verifies the one-retry bound, the shared deadline, the gate re-check, and no retry for lost, rate-limited, malformed and permanent failures.

`tests/repair/loop-live-inputs-retry_test.ts:163-219` runs the real repair cycle over 60 unchanged records with one injected 502: one extra GraphQL request instead of fallback, 60 `unchanged_inputs` skips, and no repair-state write.
`src/host/throughput-watchdog-thresholds.ts` is unchanged and the diff touches no review, CI, P0 or accounting gate; the live median reduction is left to the task 10-cycle re-measurement.
